catalog_quote: Phonemic stress with a low functional load has been reported to occur in at least Yekora, Baruga, and Korafe. Examples from the Tafota dialect of Baruga from Farr and Farr (2004:10) follow. ... The first form of each pair follows the default stress pattern apparent in the language and the latter of each pair deviates from it. [p.80] In the case of Proto Binandere, penultimate stress is assumed for two- and three-syllable words (at least in the case of non-verbs), based on the analyses of stress in the present-day languages; Suena, Zia, Binandere, Hunjara, Tafota Baruga, and Korafe all exhibit this pattern. An alternative set of stress rules appears to exist for verbs in the daughter languages. [p.13 source table:] Yekora ... Wilson 1988a phonology statement [Appendix, set 139 pBin *sinə 'dog'] 02Yek ina n dog DW69 78 / 02Yek i'na n dog DW88 - [set 305 pBin *inua 'moon'] 02Yek ina n moon DW69 78 / 02Yek 'ina n moon DW88 - [Wilson 1969:78 note 2] Yekora 'dog' and 'moon', ina, ina, are different in tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Yekora is reported (second-hand, after Wilson 1988a) to have phonemic (contrastive) word stress with low functional load, exemplified by i'na 'dog' vs 'ina 'moon'; no default stress position is stated for Yekora itself (it is absent from Smallhorn's list of penultimate-stress Binanderean languages), though sister languages are described as penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the minimal pair i'na 'dog' / 'ina 'moon' (Wilson 1969:78 had described the same pair as differing 'in tone').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms (disyllabic nouns) in a comparative wordlist; family-wide note that verbs follow different stress rules (stress on first syllable of TAM suffix in Binandere, Korafe) but nothing Yekora-specific.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to Yekora [ykr] = yeko1240 (villages Sapa, Ana, Posei, Morobe Province); no dialect distinction. The stress data trace to Darryl Wilson's SIL fieldwork (1969 survey, 1975 word list, 1988 preliminary phonology).

sources.note: Sec. 3.6 Suprasegmentals p.79: 'Phonemic stress with a low functional load has been reported to occur in at least Yekora, Baruga, and Korafe' (second-hand; Yekora phonology source is Wilson 1988a, listed p.13). p.80: the list of daughter languages with penultimate stress (Suena, Zia, Binandere, Hunjara, Tafota Baruga, Korafe) does NOT include Yekora. Appendix cognate sets 139 (p.216) and 305 (p.287) cite Yekora i'na 'dog' vs 'ina 'moon' from DW88 = Wilson 1988a, a stress-placement minimal pair. No Yekora stress rule stated.
